key_insight: An AI system can change even when its public name stays the same. The authors argue that meaningful version identifiers are needed to make these changes visible to researchers and regulators.
problem_solved: Providers update models and system integrations without updating public identifiers, making it difficult to reproduce research results or track which system was subject to regulatory oversight.
method: Identify the accountability and reproducibility risks of changing AI systems under unchanged public identifiers.
Argue for meaningful versioning that reflects updates to models and their system integrations.
Frame versioning around the needs of researchers and regulators.
impact: Meaningful versioning could help practitioners track the systems they evaluate and deploy, compare results reliably, and support regulatory oversight. The abstract presents a call for better versioning, not a tested implementation.
visual_elements: Before-and-after diagram: one unchanged public model name concealing two different underlying systems.
Version timeline showing model and integration updates alongside distinct version identifiers.
Reproducibility icon: a research experiment linked to a specific AI system version.
Oversight diagram connecting a version identifier to researchers, providers, and regulators.
paper_authors: Vasilios Mavroudis, Dan Ristea, Lauritz Morlock, Carlos Mougan
